newsitem.title: USA: MGE spring wheat ends mostly lower, new lows set.
newsitem.headline: MGE spring wheat ends mostly lower, new lows set.

text.p: MGE spring wheat futures settled mostly lower and just above new contract lows as U.S. wheat markets were hit by technical selling and jitters over an apparent resumption of EU export subsidies, traders said.
But MGE wheat did not slip as much as its counterparts in Chicago and Kansas City, thanks to continued mill demand.
"We saw good (mill) buying on our lows and not as much technical selling as they had in Chicago," a trader said.
One trader said farmers have started to sell some lower-quality spring wheat, which had put a slight squeeze on mills who were still looking for high-quality supplies.

MGE spring wheat closed 6-1/2 cents per bushel lower to one cent higher, with Sept expiring down three cents at $4.23. Dec closed down 4-1/4 cents at $4.06-1/4. March set a new contract low at $4.06 before closing at $4.07-1/2, down 6-1/2.

Benson Quinn sold 1.5 million Dec bushels and LFG sold 1.5 million March, traders said. CIS bought 800,000 each of March and Dec. MGE estimated Thursday's spring wheat futures volume at 20.782 million bushels, versus 26.262 million on Wednesday.
MGE barley futures ended two to four cents per hundredweight lower, with Dec down two cents at $7.15.
